set_aside.subject: K-05 admission evaluation
set_aside.text: “Admission is one recorded verdict over the whole active corpus”
set_aside.question: When an implementation can produce different results on repeated executions, which executions determine the recorded admission verdict?
options: Run every active case exactly once and decide from those executions
Run cases more than once and define how differing results are combined
set_aside.default_guess: Run each active case once in a fresh sandbox and record the verdict from exactly those executions.

witness.initial: A corpus has one case expecting value X; an implementation sometimes returns X and sometimes Y through an undetected source of chance.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
outcomes: The kernel executes the case once, happens to receive X, and records admitted.
The kernel executes it more than once, observes Y on one execution, and records refused.
witness.observer: The authoring agent sees whether the implementation is activated.

set_aside.subject: Repeated submission of equal implementation content
set_aside.text: “Admission is one recorded verdict” and “admit and activate | kernel, when an implementation is submitted”
set_aside.question: When equal content returns the existing implementation and is submitted again against the same corpus, must the kernel return the existing verdict or perform and record another admission attempt?
options: Perform a new attempt and replace the verdict
Perform a new attempt and retain multiple verdicts
set_aside.default_guess: Reuse an immutable verdict keyed by the implementation and exact corpus.

witness.initial: A nondeterministic implementation already has a refused verdict over the current corpus although another execution could pass.
events: The authoring agent submits byte-for-byte equal code for the same contract version again.
outcomes: The kernel returns the existing refused verdict because there is one recorded verdict.
The kernel runs admission again, this execution passes, and it records admitted and activates the implementation.
witness.observer: The authoring agent sees whether the same implementation becomes active.

set_aside.subject: Admission after trial-corpus growth
set_aside.text: “one recorded verdict over the whole active corpus”
set_aside.question: When a case is added after an implementation was admitted and activated, what happens to its recorded verdict and activation?
options: The old verdict remains historical and the activation remains usable until a new admission is requested
The kernel automatically evaluates the enlarged corpus and replaces or supplements the verdict
The old verdict immediately ceases to authorize use and the activation is removed or disabled
set_aside.default_guess: The old verdict remains historical but is not a verdict over the current corpus; adding the case does not silently change the activation, and a new admission must be triggered explicitly.

witness.initial: Implementation I is admitted and active over corpus {A}.
events: An authoring agent adds case B, which I would fail.
An owner or agent starts a flow whose function node uses I.
outcomes: The run starts and executes I because its existing activation remains in force.
The start is refused, or I is no longer active, because its verdict is not over the now-active corpus {A,B}.
witness.observer: The flow caller sees whether a run is created.

set_aside.subject: Recorded admission verdict storage and inspection
set_aside.question: What record owns the verdict, what identifies the implementation and corpus it covers, and through which inspect output can an owner or agent retrieve it later?
options: The verdict is part of the implementation's typed description
The verdict is trial evidence and is returned through inspection of trial evidence
The verdict is an internal record used by activation and rollback but is not inspectable
set_aside.default_guess: Store an immutable admission record keyed by implementation identity and corpus identity, and expose it with the implementation's typed inspection output.

witness.initial: An implementation was admitted, then another implementation became active for the same contract version.
events: A different authoring agent later inspects the slot before requesting rollback.
outcomes: Inspection exposes the earlier implementation's admitted verdict and the exact corpus it covers, so the agent can determine whether rollback is eligible.
Inspection exposes no admission record; eligibility is known only by attempting rollback and observing refusal or success.
witness.observer: The later authoring agent sees whether admission history is inspectable.
